title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
subtitle: Minimizing key movement when nodes join, fail, or scale
overview: Naive modulo partitioning (`hash(key) % N`) remaps almost every key whenever a cache or database node is added or crashes, triggering massive cache miss avalanches. Consistent Hashing maps both servers and keys onto a 0..2^32-1 hash ring using Virtual Nodes (vnodes) so adding/removing 1 node moves only ~K/N keys.
firstPrinciplesStory: You shard 100 million user profiles across 10 cache servers using `hash(user_id) % 10`. Everything runs smoothly until Server #4 overheats on Friday afternoon and drops out. Changing the divisor from 10 to 9 changes the remainder for ~90% of all keys! Overnight, 90 million cache lookups turn into misses, slamming your primary database straight into collapse. Consistent Hashing solves that exact topological fragility by decoupling key positions from the total node count.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: Imagine seats around a circular clock face (`0` to `12`). Each server puts 150 colored name tags randomly around the clock. To find who owns a key, find its number on the clock and walk clockwise until you hit the first tag. If one server disappears, only the guests sitting right before its tags shift clockwise to the next tag—everyone else stays put.
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: Both server vnodes (`shard-a#0..149`) and keys pass through a uniform hash (MurmurHash3 / xxHash) into a sorted 32-bit integer array. Routing binary-searches clockwise in `O(log V)`. Removing a node deletes its vnode slices, shifting only `~K/N` keys evenly across all remaining neighbors.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: Consistent hashing with vnodes guarantees even key *counts*, NOT even *QPS*—a viral celebrity profile still hashes to one single vnode and melts that shard! Mitigate hot keys via key salting (`celeb:id#0..7`) or local in-process L1 caches; note also that hash partitioning sacrifices efficient range scans (DDIA Ch. 6).

ddiaAnchors.concept: Hash Partitioning, Skew & Fixed Logical Partitions
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Explains why modulo hashing breaks on resize and how virtual nodes/fixed logical slots keep rebalancing bounded.

pragmaticTips.tip: Hardcoding `N` inside a modulo formula couples every stored key to static cluster capacity—design partition placement to survive elastic scaling.
pragmaticTips.application: Use virtual nodes (150–200/node) or fixed logical hash slots (like Redis's 16,384 slots) before cluster growth demands it.

keyTakeaways: Modulo hashing remaps ~(N-1)/N keys on cluster resize; consistent hashing remaps only ~1/N keys.
Virtual nodes (e.g., 150–200 tokens per physical server) prevent non-uniform data skew and smooth heterogeneous hardware.
Hot keys (celebrities) still saturate a single shard unless mitigated by key salting or local L1 caching.

nodes.label: Partition Router
nodes.summary: Hashes incoming key onto 32-bit ring and binary-searches clockwise for first vnode.
failureModes: Stale ring topology view during rapid node membership churn

nodes.label: Hash Ring Directory
nodes.summary: Logical sorted array of virtual token positions pointing to physical storage shards.
whenToUse: Mapping keys deterministically without a centralized lookup hop
failureModes: Split ring views cause temporary read misses until gossip converges

nodes.label: Cache Shard A
nodes.summary: Physical node owning 150 distributed intervals across the hash ring.
failureModes: Hardware crash shifts its vnodes clockwise to immediate neighbors

nodes.label: Cache Shard B
failureModes: Hot key skew if one tenant exceeds single-shard NIC

nodes.label: Cache Shard C
nodes.summary: Physical node owning 150 interleaved intervals (plus fallback for Shard B clockwise).
failureModes: Receives extra load when clockwise predecessor fails

steps.payloadInspector: Key: session:u_9402 -> Ring Pos: 0x7F9C3216 -> Binary Search 450 sorted vnodes
steps.inspectorNote: Router computes a fast non-cryptographic hash in nanoseconds and performs binary search over the cached ring array.

steps.info: Next clockwise vnode is shard-b#47 (pos 2,145,000,010) -> HIT
steps.inspectorNote: Virtual nodes spread Shard B across 150 positions so standard deviation of keys per shard drops below ~5%.

predictPrompt.prompt: Why do 150 virtual nodes per physical server matter when Shard B crashes, compared to putting only 1 point per server on the ring?
predictPrompt.hint: Look at who absorbs Shard B's orphaned keys in both cases.
predictPrompt.reveal: With only 1 point per server, Shard B's entire 33% traffic shifts onto ONE neighbor (doubling Shard C's load and potentially cascading). With 150 interleaved vnodes, Shard B's load splits ~50/50 across Shard A and Shard C.

chaosScenarios.title: Shard B Crashes (Minimal ~33% Remap vs 100% Modulo Churn)
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Cache Shard B dies unexpectedly; gossip removes its 150 vnodes from the ring.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Only Shard B's keys walk clockwise to Shard A and Shard C (~16.5% extra load each), leaving 67% of cluster cache completely untouched.

steps.info: Shard B heartbeat missed -> 150 vnodes removed; 67% of existing keys unaffected
steps.payloadInspector: Modulo hash would invalidate ~67-99% of keys; Consistent Hash invalidates only keys owned by Shard B (~33%).
steps.inspectorNote: Vnodes distribute Shard B's orphaned keys evenly across BOTH Shard A and Shard C instead of overloading a single neighbor.

steps.info: session:u_9402 remaps clockwise to shard-c#89 -> cold miss refills cleanly
steps.payloadInspector: Re-routed to 10.0.4.13:6379 -> miss -> re-populated from DB
steps.inspectorNote: Because only K/N keys move, the origin DB easily absorbs the partial cache warm-up.

pros: Minimal K/N key movement on scaling/failure
cons: Hot keys still hit a single shard
Range scans (e.g. BETWEEN timestamps) cannot use single-shard locality

pros: Explicit 16,384 hash slots allow atomic live slot migration
cons: Needs cluster bus or config coordinator for slot-to-node table
tradeoffs.bestFor: Managed stateful clusters requiring deterministic resharding
